experiment: unique-candidate matched visual scaling stress test

candidate_pool.grid: grasp x offset by wrist yaw, shuffled independently by locked scene seed

causal_comparison: visual_world_model minus matched_no_vision; same checkpoint and candidate inputs, visual latent is the only ablation
verdict: Larger unique pools make the visual and matched arms diverge, but the predeclared visual-value interval still includes zero. The visual arm also remains below first and random at N=64, so this run does not support a useful visual ranking claim.
limitation: This is a geometric stress grid over grasp offset and yaw, not a natural-program diversity benchmark.
